### 🔍 Search Terms

declare namespace
namespace same name as generic type
type hints
type alias name
generic type arguments
hide type arguments in type hint
hide type arguments when namespace

### ✅ Viability Checklist

- [x] This wouldn't be a breaking change in existing TypeScript/JavaScript code
- [x] This wouldn't change the runtime behavior of existing JavaScript code
- [x] This could be implemented without emitting different JS based on the types of the expressions
- [x] This isn't a runtime feature (e.g. library functionality, non-ECMAScript syntax with JavaScript output, new syntax sugar for JS, etc.)
- [x] This isn't a request to add a new utility type: https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/wiki/No-New-Utility-Types
- [x] This feature would agree with the rest of our Design Goals: https://github.com/Microsoft/TypeScript/wiki/TypeScript-Design-Goals

### ⭐ Suggestion

When hinting a type in a `namespace` whose name is shared by a sibling generic type, the generic type's type arguments should not be shown in the hint.

### 📃 Motivating Example

When writing types, it's often useful to use `declare namespace` to 'nest' related utility types underneath a type's name. e.g. [ts playground](https://www.typescriptlang.org/play/?#code/C4TwDgpgBAQgTgQwHYBMA8AVKBeKBXJAayQHsB3JAPhyiwDIoBvKAfRYCNFUAuKAcgCyIDOAh8AvgChJKCAGMANgjjQkCALYQAzmARzo8ZCiaSoZqBAAeYEnGBRQkKAFUkZRGEwXLwCKi2wXCjUuFhWvv6BRmgAlkgAZhBwLtQA-C5QvEgQAG5JklKSjtAAGjSGqAB0ru4InhXofPEkJHyUlJIA9J3mvX1QAHqpQA)

```ts
export type Brand<T = unknown> = T & { __brand: 'MyType'}

export declare namespace Brand {
    export type Unwrap<T extends Brand> = T extends Brand<infer U> ? U : never
}
```

In this example, when TS provides hints for a usage of `Unwrap`, this is the hint we get:
`type Brand<T = unknown>.Unwrap<T extends Brand> = T extends Brand<infer U> ? U : never`

Since the `Brand` keyword is being used as a `namespace` in this case, the type arguments `<T = unknown>` are superfluous and just make the type hard to read.

A better hint would simply be:
`type Brand.Unwrap<T extends Brand> = T extends Brand<infer U> ? U : never`

These tidier hints make it more attractive to organize related types using `declare namespace`, by making their names and namespacing more readable.

### 💻 Use Cases

1. What do you want to use this for?

Since `declare namespace` has no runtime impact, it's a useful tool to meaningfully structure types in an intuitive and expressive way. This allows for better completion, discovery and logical scoping.

E.g. in this, we're defining a type `Ftor`, with utilities available as `Ftor.In` etc.
```
export type Ftor<A extends [...unknown[]] = never, R = unknown> = Fn<A, R> | Ctor<A, R>

export declare namespace Ftor {
  export type In<A extends [...unknown[]] = [...unknown[]]> = FnIn<A> | CtorIn<A>
  export type Out<R = unknown> = FnOut<R> | CtorOut<R>

  // Other related 'Ftor' utility types
}

```

2. What shortcomings exist with current approaches?

The only problem with using `declare namespace` in this way is that we can't read the namespacing in type hints, because (unrelated) type arguments are displayed, as shown in the Motivating example.

3. What workarounds are you using in the meantime?

None, unfortunately. Other than giving the namespace its own name.
items.title: Hide type args when hinting a type nested in a namespace of the same name as a generic type.
